https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/british-youtub.text: A British YouTuber who built a family-friendly brand on Minecraft gameplay and wholesome comedy content faces extradition to Poland over allegations of sexual activity with girls under 15. Stuart Kluz-Burton, known to his four million subscribers as Stuu, was arrested in Luton in October 2023 after Polish prosecutors issued charges relating to alleged incidents in 2015 and 2018.The UK Supreme Court upheld the extradition order on 17 July 2026, rejecting Kluz-Burton's final appeal and clearing the way for his transfer to Polish authorities. The 34-year-old, who holds dual British and Polish citizenship, now awaits transport to Warsaw to face formal charges, and has not been convicted of any of the alleged offences at this stage.Extradition Battle Concludes After Three YearsKluz-Burton faces one count of sexual touching and three additional charges connected to alleged assaults on teenagers, the Crown Prosecution Service said in its summary of the case. Two of the charges allege inducing minors to consume alcohol, according to court documents filed in Warsaw and Polish arrest warrant details.The YouTube creator was detained in the UK after Polish prosecutors sought his arrest and obtained a warrant linked to the Pandora Gate investigation, filings from the Warsaw prosecution service state. He has been fighting extradition through multiple court levels since his initial arrest three years ago, with British judges repeatedly ruling that the Polish warrant remains valid and that political commentary did not undermine judicial independence.Allegations Emerge from Pandora Gate InvestigationThe allegations came to light in October 2023 after Polish filmmaker Sylwester Wardega published a YouTube video alleging that Kluz-Burton and other creators had inappropriate relationships with underage girls, including sharing chat logs and screenshots. In subsequent coverage of the case, Kluz-Burton declined to comment on the allegations when approached, according to a report in The Independent based on his UK court appearances.Polish authorities have pursued the case as part of the wider Pandora Gate investigation into misconduct among Polish-language content creators, built on material gathered by Wardega and fellow commentator Konopskyy as well as formal complaints to prosecutors. Officials in Warsaw have described the affair as a major test of how the justice system deals with online influencers accused of targeting young fans.From Minecraft Stardom to Extradition: The Rise of a Family-Friendly ChannelFor more than a decade, Kluz-Burton has run a successful YouTube channel featuring lifestyle, comedy and gaming content primarily in Polish. One of his most-watched clips has accumulated more than 17 million views.His channel has generated more than a billion total views across all content since he began posting from Poland in the mid-2010s, the same report noted. The case has attracted significant attention given the family-oriented nature of much of his content, which prosecutors say was watched extensively by teenagers and younger viewers. Child protection advocates in both Poland and the UK have warned that channels marketed at younger audiences face particular scrutiny when such allegations emerge.How the Case Echoes Previous Online Grooming ExtraditionsThe circumstances echo previous incidents involving online personalities and child safety, including a Scottish man who admitted using Minecraft to groom children in America in 2017. Court records in Arizona show he was extradited and pleaded guilty to multiple felony charges. Polish prosecutors are continuing their investigation, with authorities urging anyone with relevant information to come forward in public statements about Pandora Gate. The Divisional Court in London previously noted that ministerial remarks aimed at Polish prosecutors did not invalidate the extradition warrant.Kluz-Burton's legal team had argued against extradition on multiple grounds, including claims of political interference, but British judges consistently found the warrant lawful and the requested offences extraditable. He is expected to be transported to Poland in the coming weeks to face trial once logistical arrangements between UK and Polish authorities are completed.

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqjx.text: Image source, KASA/Reuters By Malu Cursino Published 6 hours ago South Korea's space agency has released images that show the Moon after part of a SpaceX rocket crashed into its surface on Wednesday. The Korean AeroSpace Administration (KASA) said lunar orbiter Danubri captured images after the impact, which it shared , external alongside photos of what the Moon's surface looked like before the crash. Rocket debris struck the Moon at around 06:35 GMT on Wednesday, according to the South Korean space agency. SpaceX has said the impact was not intentional. Image source, KASA/Reuters Re-usable Falcon 9 rockets were designed to allow part of the rocket to return to Earth (the upper stage) and other sections to be shed in space. SpaceX has used this type of rocket on several missions. The empty upper stage of this Falcon 9 rocket, which scientists predicted would hit the Moon at a speed of about 5,400mph (8,700km/h), is about the size of a five-storey building and weighs approximately 4,000kg (630st) on Earth. The short, dramatic flash created when the rocket part hit the Moon would have been hard to catch by amateur astronomers even with high-end telescopes, but larger observatories - including Seoul's space agency - are analysing the information. While the impact did not pose any danger to Earth, Matt Bothwell, astronomer at the University of Cambridge, raised concerns about space debris. "Space is getting more and more crowded," he said, as each year "we launch more stuff into space". "It could feasibly be within a few decades that it's actually quite hard to get past Earth's orbit because space is so crowded," Bothwell warned. This Falcon 9 was in orbit since January last year, when it blasted off from Florida. The same booster section from the January 2025 mission is due to set off on its 18th flight on 10 August. SpaceX says the mission hopes to launch 29 Starlink satellites to low-Earth orbit. The rocket that blasted from Florida last January was carrying two lunar landers into space. Its job was to fire the upper stage hard enough to send both of the landers out of Earth's orbit and onto a path towards the Moon. The spent stage was left drifting in a long, looping orbit that swung out towards the Moon and back again. Over the next 18 months, the gentle gravitational tug of the Earth, Moon and Sun, along with light from the Sun, gave it a faint push. Astronomers tracking the rocket part eventually worked out that those small nudges had put it on a course towards the Moon, and it was picking up speed every day. The impact on Wednesday happened in broad daylight for many parts of the world, but the tiny flash it produced would have been far too faint to see, even through a telescope. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: 2:02 Timeline of how deadly Nepal and Tibet flash flood unfolded – explainer Nepal-Tibet flood disaster Nepal-Tibet flood rescue efforts resume after being halted by overflowing lake Risk of fresh flooding had forced rescue teams to withdraw as residents rushed up hills to escape possible river surge Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates Visual guide: how the deadly flooding unfolded Tell us: have you been affected by the flash floods? Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Bidur, Sam Jones and agencies Fri 28 Aug 2026 06.17 EDT First published on Fri 28 Aug 2026 01.45 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Rescuers searching for survivors of deadly flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have resumed their efforts after suspending operations when a debris dam burst its bank on Friday, increasing the risk of fresh flooding. Residents in Nepal’s Rasuwa district, on the border with Tibet, were seen rushing up hillsides ⁠on Friday to escape a possible surge in the river, ⁠according to witnesses. Fears of another flood came as authorities in Nepal and China said that at least 543 people had been killed in the disaster. Barrier lake forms at base of mountains near Nepal border More than 500 foreign citizens were among 826 people missing in Nepal , police and tourism ⁠officials said, including 177 from India, 90 from the US, 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain and 25 from Canada. Chinese state media said at least 558 were missing on the Tibet side of the border, of whom at least 260 were foreign nationals. Climate crisis could be destabilising mountain areas like Nepal, experts warn Read more The flood on Wednesday had destroyed power stations, roads and bridges along a route that links Kathmandu with Lhasa in Tibet and is ⁠popular with trekkers and pilgrims. The Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that a lake formed by piles of debris from the mudslide had begun overflowing on Friday, sending water towards the area where rescue teams were headed, and forcing a brief pause in operations. Rescue efforts in Bidur, the capital of the Nuwakot district in Bagmati province, Nepal, were disrupted on Friday morning as the the Trishuli River began to rise again after the lake near the China border burst its banks. 10:11 ‘Erased before their eyes’: on the ground in decimated Nepal flood zone - The Latest Rescue workers were moved from the area and people who had tried to return to what remained of their homes were told to evacuate again immediately. Bidur, once a bustling town on the banks of the Trishuli, now lies in ruins. Most homes were washed away when a tide of mud, rocks and debris surged down the river valley early on Wednesday. Survivors described clinging to buildings and trees as the water rushed over them. The mangled concrete remains of a bank, a government office and an ATM booth were among the few structures left standing, although they were submerged in mud. Officials said there were still bodies inside the buildings but it was too dangerous to recover them. Nearby, local people gathered along the muddy road, calling out for lost relatives and trying to dig out what was left of their belongings. Most areas battered by flash floods remained accessible only by army helicopter. At the Bidur army camp, where much of the rescue effort was being coordinated, rescue and military helicopters flew in and out every five minutes, bringing in dozens of traumatised victims. Many said that in a matter of minutes, the floods had taken their loved ones, their homes and everything they owned. The international community is scrambling to get aid to flood-stricken parts of Nepal and Tibet. View image in fullscreen Sludge inundates homes after flash floods in Nuwakot district. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images Nepal has said it does not yet need foreign assistance as the search-and-rescue operation – complicated by the destruction of dozens of bridges and miles of roads across the mountainous region – continues. “The offer for help is natural,” Lok Bahadur Chhetri, a spokesperson for Nepal’s foreign ministry, said on Friday. “Our security agencies ‌are doing the search and rescue operation. For now we don’t require such help.” The Kathmandu Post reported that India, China, the US, Britain, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh had asked the government to allow their search-and-rescue teams to assist in the operation. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to This is India Niha Masih takes a look at the stories, ideas and news makers of modern India after newsletter promotion Dinesh Bhattarai, a former Nepali ⁠ambassador to the UN in Geneva, said the government’s reluctance to ​accept foreign assistance may ​be linked to sensitivities over ​Rasuwa district and its border with China’s Tibet region. “They may have thought about ​the locational sensitivity ‌of the region and ​decided not to ​accept foreign teams,” Bhattarai told Reuters. But Chhetri said Nepal’s own rescue teams were handling the operation and the decision to refuse foreign assistance had nothing to do with sensitivities involving China. Scant information has emerged from Chinese authorities about the scale of the destruction in Tibet, the most tightly controlled part of China even under normal circumstances. Only brief, state-controlled media reports about the floods have been allowed to circulate in China and the authorities have confirmed only three deaths there. Chinese reports have focused on rescue efforts. In Nepal earlier on Friday, army helicopter rescue teams were working to free about 100 people trapped in a tunnel at a flooded hydropower project. Map showing location of the disaster “Our focus is in search and rescue of people … some people are trapped in the tunnel of Trishuli 3A hydropower project,” said the Nepal army spokesperson, Raja Ram Basnet. “Two helicopters have been dispatched but it is challenging because it is tough to even locate the entry points of the tunnel. Relief efforts are also under way to provide the rescued people what they need.” The prime minister’s office said the army was working in challenging conditions and had rescued 350 workers and local people who were trapped in the tunnel. Rescue teams reported finding bodies hundreds of miles downstream from the disaster zone in the Chitwan district of Nepal, near the Tibetan border. Dozens of injured people were transported to Kathmandu for advanced medical care and more than 100 people were rescued by Nepali army personnel in helicopters. CCTV said 499 Chinese nationals and 555 foreigners had been transported out of the disaster zone as of Friday. https://www.theguardian.com/business/202.text: The market value of Shell rose to a record high of £36.23 a share at the end of last month. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images View image in fullscreen The market value of Shell rose to a record high of £36.23 a share at the end of last month. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images Shell Shell expects refineries to almost double the profit from every barrel of fuel made Record prices caused by global shortages amid shutdown of war-damaged refineries in Middle East and Russia Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent Wed 7 Oct 2026 04.30 EDT Last modified on Wed 7 Oct 2026 08.04 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Shell’s refineries are expected to make record profits on each barrel of fuel produced after shortages in the global market caused pump prices around the world to climb to all-time highs. In a trading update on Wednesday, the energy supermajor forecast profit margins of $42 a barrel in the July to September period, far above the margins of $24 a barrel in the second quarter. The forecast margins are also significantly higher than the previous record for petroleum products of about $28 a barrel, set in the early months of the Russia-Ukraine war. The margins reflect the steep increase in the price of refined fuels, including diesel, relative to the cost of the crude oil. A partial recovery of Gulf oil exports has allowed crude market prices to ease back to about $100 a barrel, while war damage to refineries in the Middle East and Russia has caused fuel prices to continue to climb. That gap should make larger profits possible for refineries, particularly those in the US and Europe. The Middle East crisis has already helped Shell to a profit of almost $10bn (£7.5bn) for the second quarter of 2026, more than double the figure for the same period last year and its second highest quarterly earnings on record. The market value of Europe’s biggest oil and gas company, now the second largest company on the UK’s FTSE 100 index, climbed to a record high of £36.23 a share at the end of last month. That share price was reached despite oil prices retreating from their 2026 peak of above $115 a barrel in spring to about $100. It was lifted by European gas prices, which doubled from the previous year over the summer, and record high diesel prices . Global oil prices were slightly lower in the third quarter of the year. Brent crude averaged $85.60 a barrel, compared with $97.05 in the second quarter, but still well above the $68.14 recorded in the third quarter last year. The diesel price premium over the global oil benchmark jumped above $100 a barrel for the first time, indicating record high profits from refining crude into fuels. Shell operates some of Europe’s largest refineries alongside the French energy company TotalEnergies, which has the continent’s largest refining capacity. TotalEnergies’ chief executive, Patrick Pouyanné, welcomed the opportunities created by the global energy crisis. He told an industry conference in London this week: “We’re doing really well by being integrated. Integration means your refineries in Europe, which you thought were liabilities, are suddenly becoming goldmines.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Business Today Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning after newsletter promotion Europe’s benchmark gas price index more than doubled to €70.50 (£60) in August. The price of gas reached an average of more than €48 a megawatt-hour in the second quarter before leaping to almost €64/MWh in the third quarter. Shell’s gas production has been hard hit by the Middle East crisis, which led to severe damage to one of its key gas processing facilities in the Gulf, cutting its prewar gas production of 900,000 barrels ⁠of oil ​equivalent ‌per day (BOED) by a third. Shell said on Wednesday that it expected gas production to climb to about 740,000 to 780,000 barrels ⁠of oil ​equivalent ‌a day ‌after its acquisition of Canada’s ARC Resources, up sharply from its previous forecast of 570,000 to 630,000 BOED for the quarter. It produced about 631,000 BOED in the second quarter. The deal, which is expected to add about 370,000 barrels a day to Shell’s production of oil and gas, was completed in early September to add a month’s worth of production to its estimates for the quarter.
